Request reprint permissions here.In the span of a few years, China and the United States have each assembled something future historians might recognize as a new kind of empire. Their dominions extend not merely over territory, trade routes, and airspace but over knowledge itself. By controlling the large language models, chips, physical infrastructure, and capital that provide the foundations for advanced machine cognition, Beijing and Washington are not only attaining new heights of economic performance and power projection; they are also setting the terms of all future scientific and intellectual progress. NIALL FERGUSON is Milbank Family Senior Fellow at the Hoover Institution at Stanford University and the author of Empire: The Rise and Demise of the British World Order.LISA KLAASSEN is a doctoral candidate at the Oxford Internet Institute and a Fellow at the Tarbell Center for AI Journalism.ERIC SCHMIDT is Chair of the Special Competitive Studies Project and former CEO and Chair of Google.
